907	# Build the complete Claude Code role profile for a selected main model. Native
908	# Claude profiles use the strongest served model in each family. OpenAI profiles
909	# map quality/balanced/fast work to the selected main, Terra and Luna.
910	function script:Get-CopilotModelProfile {
911	    param([string] $Model = (Get-CopilotDefaultModel), $Catalog)
912	    if (-not $PSBoundParameters.ContainsKey('Catalog')) { $Catalog = Get-CopilotModelCatalog }
913	    $models = Get-CopilotCatalogIds $Catalog
914	    $raw = Remove-CopilotContextHint $Model
915	    $main = ConvertTo-CopilotClaudeModel -Model $Model -Catalog $Catalog
916	
917	    $fableRaw = $raw; $opusRaw = $raw; $sonnetRaw = $raw; $haikuRaw = $raw
918	    if ($raw -like 'claude-*') {
919	        $fableRaw = Select-CopilotFirstServed -Model $models -Candidate @('claude-fable-5')
920	        if (-not $fableRaw) { $fableRaw = @($models | Where-Object { $_ -like 'claude-fable-*' } | Sort-Object)[-1] }
921	        if (-not $fableRaw) { $fableRaw = $raw }
922	
923	        $opusRaw = Select-CopilotFirstServed -Model $models -Candidate @(
924	            'claude-opus-5', 'claude-opus-4-8', 'claude-opus-4-7', 'claude-opus-4-6', 'claude-opus-4-5'
925	        )
926	        if (-not $opusRaw) { $opusRaw = @($models | Where-Object { $_ -like 'claude-opus-*' } | Sort-Object)[-1] }
927	        if (-not $opusRaw) { $opusRaw = $raw }
928	
929	        $sonnetRaw = Select-CopilotFirstServed -Model $models -Candidate @(
930	            'claude-sonnet-5', 'claude-sonnet-4-6', 'claude-sonnet-4-5'
931	        )
932	        if (-not $sonnetRaw) { $sonnetRaw = @($models | Where-Object { $_ -like 'claude-sonnet-*' } | Sort-Object)[-1] }
933	        if (-not $sonnetRaw) { $sonnetRaw = $raw }
934	
935	        $haikuRaw = Select-CopilotFirstServed -Model $models -Candidate @('claude-haiku-4-5')
936	        if (-not $haikuRaw) { $haikuRaw = @($models | Where-Object { $_ -like 'claude-haiku-*' } | Sort-Object)[-1] }
937	        if (-not $haikuRaw) { $haikuRaw = $raw }
938	    }
939	    elseif ($raw -like 'gpt-*' -or $raw -match 'codex') {
940	        $sonnetRaw = Select-CopilotFirstServed -Model $models -Candidate @('gpt-5.6-terra')
941	        if (-not $sonnetRaw) { $sonnetRaw = $raw }
942	        $haikuRaw = Select-CopilotFirstServed -Model $models -Candidate @('gpt-5.6-luna', 'gpt-5.4-mini', 'gpt-5-mini')
943	        if (-not $haikuRaw) { $haikuRaw = $raw }
944	    }
945	
946	    [ordered]@{
947	        main   = $main
948	        fable  = ConvertTo-CopilotClaudeModel -Model $fableRaw -Catalog $Catalog
949	        opus   = ConvertTo-CopilotClaudeModel -Model $opusRaw -Catalog $Catalog
950	        sonnet = ConvertTo-CopilotClaudeModel -Model $sonnetRaw -Catalog $Catalog
951	        haiku  = ConvertTo-CopilotClaudeModel -Model $haikuRaw -Catalog $Catalog
952	    }
953	}

964	# "<model>|<source>" — the model Claude Code would send from this directory.
965	function script:Get-CopilotEffectiveModel {
966	    param([string] $Settings = '.claude/settings.local.json')
967	    $settings = $Settings
968	    if (Test-Path $settings) {
969	        try {
970	            $j = Get-Content -Raw $settings | ConvertFrom-Json
971	            if ($j.env.ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL) {
972	                $m = $j.env.ANTHROPIC_MODEL
973	                if ($m) { return "$m|project pin: $settings" }
974	                return "|project pin missing ANTHROPIC_MODEL: $settings"
975	            }
976	        } catch { $null = $_ }
977	    }
978	    if ($env:COPILOT_CLAUDE_MODEL) { return "$($env:COPILOT_CLAUDE_MODEL)|`$COPILOT_CLAUDE_MODEL" }
979	    $sf = Get-CopilotModelState
980	    if (Test-Path $sf) { return "$(Get-Content -First 1 $sf)|state file: $sf" }
981	    "$(Get-CopilotDefaultModel)|built-in default"
982	}

984	# The EXACT env block `copilot-here on` / `copilot-run` would apply right now.
985	#
986	# SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for three callers: copilot-run (process env),
987	# `copilot-here on` (what it merges into settings.local.json) and
988	# Get-CopilotHereDrift (what it compares against). These used to be hand-maintained
989	# copies and they diverged — the drift check compared 4 of the 8 keys `on` writes,
990	# so a pin missing ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_HAIKU_MODEL / ANTHROPIC_SMALL_FAST_MODEL /
991	# CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC reported "no drift" while `on` would
992	# still have changed it. Add a key here and all three follow.
993	#
994	# -Pinned uses the shim base when the shim is enabled but not yet up (what a
995	# written-to-disk pin should say); copilot-run wants the live base instead.
996	function script:Get-CopilotEnvBlock {
997	    param([switch] $Pinned, [string] $Model = (Get-CopilotDefaultModel), $Catalog)
998	    $modelProfile = if ($PSBoundParameters.ContainsKey('Catalog')) {
999	        Get-CopilotModelProfile -Model $Model -Catalog $Catalog
1000	    } else {
1001	        Get-CopilotModelProfile -Model $Model
1002	    }
1003	    $block = [ordered]@{
1004	        ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL             = if ($Pinned) { Get-CopilotPinnedBase } else { Get-CopilotClientBase }
1005	        ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN           = 'dummy'
1006	        ANTHROPIC_MODEL                = $modelProfile.main
1007	        ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_FABLE_MODEL  = $modelProfile.fable
1008	        ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL   = $modelProfile.opus
1009	        ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_SONNET_MODEL = $modelProfile.sonnet
1010	        ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_HAIKU_MODEL  = $modelProfile.haiku
1011	        ANTHROPIC_SMALL_FAST_MODEL     = $modelProfile.haiku
1012	        CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC = '1'
1013	    }
1014	    if ($env:COPILOT_PROXY_QUIET -eq '1') {
1015	        $block.CLAUDE_CODE_ATTRIBUTION_HEADER = '0'
1016	        $block.CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_PROMPT_SUGGESTION = 'false'
1017	        $block.CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_AWAY_SUMMARY = '0'
1018	        $block.DISABLE_NON_ESSENTIAL_MODEL_CALLS = '1'
1019	    }
1020	    $block
1021	}

1023	# --- shim start/stop ---
1024	function script:Start-CopilotShim {
1025	    if (Test-CopilotShimAlive) { return $true }
1026	    if (-not (Get-Command bun -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)) {
1027	        Write-Error "copilot-proxy: shim needs 'bun' (scoop install bun)"; return $false
1028	    }
1029	    $script = Get-CopilotShimScript
1030	    if (-not (Test-Path $script)) { Write-Error "copilot-proxy: shim script not found at $script"; return $false }
1031	    $env:COPILOT_SHIM_PORT = Get-CopilotShimPort
1032	    $env:COPILOT_SHIM_UPSTREAM = Get-CopilotBase
1033	    $p = Start-Process -FilePath 'bun' -ArgumentList @($script) -PassThru -WindowStyle Hidden `
1034	        -RedirectStandardOutput (Get-CopilotShimLog) -RedirectStandardError "$(Get-CopilotShimLog).err"
1035	    $p.Id | Set-Content -Path (Get-CopilotShimPid)
1036	    for ($i = 0; $i -lt 10; $i++) { if (Test-CopilotShimAlive) { return $true }; Start-Sleep 1 }
1037	    Write-Error "copilot-proxy: shim did not come up — check $(Get-CopilotShimLog)"; $false
1038	}
1039	function script:Stop-CopilotShim {
1040	    $pidf = Get-CopilotShimPid
1041	    if (Test-Path $pidf) {
1042	        $pid_ = Get-Content -First 1 $pidf -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
1043	        if ($pid_) { Stop-Process -Id $pid_ -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue }
1044	        Remove-Item $pidf -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
1045	    }
1046	    Get-CimInstance Win32_Process -Filter "Name = 'bun.exe'" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
1047	        Where-Object { $_.CommandLine -like '*copilot-throttle-shim.js*' } |
1048	        ForEach-Object { Stop-Process -Id $_.ProcessId -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue }
1049	}

1051	# ============================================================ copilot-proxy ===
1052	function copilot-proxy {
1053	    [CmdletBinding()]
1054	    param([Parameter(ValueFromRemainingArguments)] [string[]] $Argv)
1055	
1056	    if (-not (Get-Command bun -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)) {
1057	        Write-Error "copilot-proxy: bun not found (scoop install bun)"; return
1058	    }
1059	
1060	    $port = Get-CopilotPort; $pkg = Get-CopilotPkg
1061	    $logf = Get-CopilotLogFile; $pidf = Get-CopilotPidFile
1062	    $action = if ($Argv -and $Argv.Count -ge 1) { $Argv[0] } else { 'status' }
1063	
1064	    switch ($action) {
1065	        'start' {
1066	            if (Test-CopilotAlive) { Write-Host "copilot-proxy: already running on port $port"; return }
1067	            if (-not (Test-Path (Get-CopilotToken))) {
1068	                Write-Error "copilot-proxy: not authenticated yet — run 'copilot-proxy auth' first."; return
1069	            }
1070	            # Rotate the previous session's log (keep last 3).
1071	            if (Test-Path $logf) {
1072	                Remove-Item "$logf.3" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
1073	                if (Test-Path "$logf.2") { Move-Item -Force "$logf.2" "$logf.3" }
1074	                if (Test-Path "$logf.1") { Move-Item -Force "$logf.1" "$logf.2" }
1075	                Move-Item -Force $logf "$logf.1"
1076	            }
1077	            # Install the pinned package BEFORE launching anything. Resolving it at
1078	            # launch (the old `bunx <pkg> start`) is what used to hang forever behind
1079	            # a socks proxy, with nothing but "Resolving dependencies" in the log.
1080	            if (-not (Install-CopilotPkg)) { return }
1081	            $launch = Get-CopilotPkgLaunch
1082	            if (-not $launch) { Write-Error "copilot-proxy: no runnable copilot-api after install"; return }
1083	
1084	            # Node ignores the Windows System Proxy — it only honours HTTP(S)_PROXY,
1085	            # and the fork additionally needs --proxy-env before its fetch uses them.
1086	            $httpProxy = Resolve-CopilotHttpProxy
1087	            if ($httpProxy) {
1088	                Write-Host "copilot-proxy: Node will fetch /models via $httpProxy (--proxy-env; COPILOT_HTTP_PROXY=$(if ($env:COPILOT_HTTP_PROXY) { $env:COPILOT_HTTP_PROXY } else { 'auto' }))"
1089	            } elseif ($env:COPILOT_HTTP_PROXY -in 'always', 'on', '1', 'true', 'yes') {
1090	                Write-Warning "copilot-proxy: COPILOT_HTTP_PROXY=always but no proxy detected — starting DIRECT (the Claude catalog may be geo-filtered)."
1091	                Write-Host "  hint: enable the Clash/Verge System Proxy, or set COPILOT_HTTP_PROXY=http://127.0.0.1:7897"
1092	            }
1093	
1094	            $argList = @($launch.Pre + @('start', '--port', $port))
1095	            if ((Get-CopilotPkgFlavor) -eq 'original') {
1096	                $rate = if ($env:COPILOT_PROXY_RATE) { $env:COPILOT_PROXY_RATE } else { '15' }
1097	                # Original package: HTTPS_PROXY alone is enough (it has no --proxy-env).
1098	                $argList += @('--rate-limit', $rate, '--wait')
1099	                Write-Host "copilot-proxy: starting ($pkg) on port $port (rate-limit ${rate}s) ..."
1100	            } else {
1101	                if ($httpProxy) { $argList += '--proxy-env' }
1102	                Write-Host "copilot-proxy: starting ($pkg) on port $port ..."
1103	            }
1104	
1105	            # Scope the proxy env to the child: set, spawn, restore.
1106	            $proxyVars = 'HTTP_PROXY', 'HTTPS_PROXY', 'http_proxy', 'https_proxy'
1107	            $saved = @{}
1108	            if ($httpProxy) {
1109	                foreach ($v in $proxyVars) { $saved[$v] = [Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable($v); Set-Item "env:$v" $httpProxy }
1110	            }
1111	            try {
1112	                $spArgs = @{
1113	                    FilePath                = $launch.Exe
1114	                    ArgumentList            = $argList
1115	                    PassThru                = $true
1116	                    WindowStyle             = 'Hidden'
1117	                    RedirectStandardOutput  = $logf
1118	                    RedirectStandardError   = "$logf.err"
1119	                }
1120	                if ($launch.Cwd) { $spArgs.WorkingDirectory = $launch.Cwd }
1121	                $p = Start-Process @spArgs
1122	            } finally {
1123	                if ($httpProxy) {
1124	                    foreach ($v in $proxyVars) {
1125	                        if ($null -eq $saved[$v]) { Remove-Item "env:$v" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue }
1126	                        else { Set-Item "env:$v" $saved[$v] }
1127	                    }
1128	                }
1129	            }
1130	            $p.Id | Set-Content -Path $pidf
1131	            $startTimeout = if ($env:COPILOT_PROXY_START_TIMEOUT) { [int]$env:COPILOT_PROXY_START_TIMEOUT } else { 45 }
1132	            for ($i = 0; $i -lt $startTimeout; $i++) {
1133	                if (Test-CopilotAlive) {
1134	                    if (Get-CopilotShimEnabled) {
1135	                        if (Start-CopilotShim) { Write-Host "copilot-proxy: throttle shim up -> $(Get-CopilotShimBase) (-> $(Get-CopilotBase))" }
1136	                    }
1137	                    Write-Host "copilot-proxy: up -> $(Get-CopilotClientBase)  (logs: copilot-proxy logs)"
1138	                    return
1139	                }
1140	                # Crashed on its own (bad flag, port taken, auth) — don't sit out the
1141	                # remaining seconds pretending we're still waiting.
1142	                if ($p.HasExited) {
1143	                    Remove-Item $pidf -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
1144	                    Write-Error "copilot-proxy: server exited during startup — check 'copilot-proxy logs'."; return
1145	                }
1146	                Start-Sleep 1
1147	            }
1148	            # Timed out. REAP what we spawned: the old code returned and left it
1149	            # running, so each retry stacked another orphan and none ever bound the port.
1150	            Stop-Process -Id $p.Id -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
1151	            Remove-Item $pidf -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
1152	            Write-Error "copilot-proxy: did not come up in time — check 'copilot-proxy logs'."
1153	        }
1154	        'stop' {
1155	            Stop-CopilotShim
1156	            if (Test-Path $pidf) {
1157	                $pid_ = Get-Content -First 1 $pidf -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
1158	                if ($pid_) { Stop-Process -Id $pid_ -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue }
1159	                Remove-Item $pidf -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
1160	            }
1161	            Get-CimInstance Win32_Process -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
1162	                Where-Object { $_.CommandLine -like "*copilot-api*--port $port*" } |
1163	                ForEach-Object { Stop-Process -Id $_.ProcessId -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue }
1164	            Start-Sleep 1
1165	            if (Test-CopilotAlive) { Write-Error "copilot-proxy: still answering on $port (another instance?)"; return }
1166	            Write-Host "copilot-proxy: stopped (port $port free)"
1167	        }
1168	        'restart' { copilot-proxy stop; copilot-proxy start }
1169	        'status' {
1170	            if (Test-CopilotAlive) {
1171	                $catalog = Get-CopilotModelCatalog
1172	                $rawIds = Get-CopilotCatalogIds $catalog
1173	                $claude = @($rawIds | Where-Object { $_ -like 'claude-*' })
1174	                $claudeText = if ($claude.Count -gt 0) { $claude -join ' ' } else { 'none' }
1175	                Write-Host "copilot-proxy: RUNNING on $(Get-CopilotBase)"
1176	                Write-Host "  models: $($rawIds.Count) served; Claude: $claudeText"
1177	                if (Get-CopilotShimEnabled) {
1178	                    if (Test-CopilotShimAlive) { Write-Host "  shim:   ON, up on $(Get-CopilotShimBase)  -> clients use this" }
1179	                    else { Write-Host "  shim:   ON but DOWN (clients fall back to $(Get-CopilotBase))" }
1180	                } else { Write-Host "  shim:   off  (enable: copilot-proxy shim on)" }
1181	            } else {
1182	                Write-Host "copilot-proxy: not running on port $port  (start: copilot-proxy start)"
1183	            }
1184	        }
1185	        { $_ -in 'doctor', 'test' } { Invoke-CopilotDoctor -Live:($Argv -contains '--live') }
1186	        'logs' {
1187	            if ($Argv.Count -ge 2 -and $Argv[1] -eq 'shim') {
1188	                $lf = Get-CopilotShimLog; $n = if ($Argv.Count -ge 3) { [int]$Argv[2] } else { 40 }
1189	            } else {
1190	                $lf = $logf; $n = if ($Argv.Count -ge 2) { [int]$Argv[1] } else { 40 }
1191	                if ($Argv.Count -ge 3 -and $Argv[2] -in '1', '2', '3') { $lf = "$logf.$($Argv[2])" }
1192	            }
1193	            if (Test-Path $lf) { Get-Content -Tail $n $lf }
1194	            elseif (Test-Path "$lf.err") { Get-Content -Tail $n "$lf.err" }
1195	            else { Write-Error "copilot-proxy: no log file at $lf" }
1196	        }
1197	        'auth' {
1198	            # One-time device login -> stores a ghu_ token copilot-api can exchange.
1199	            Write-Host "copilot-proxy: launching copilot-api device login ..."
1200	            if ((Get-CopilotPkgFlavor) -eq 'original') { Invoke-CopilotPkgCommand auth }
1201	            else { Invoke-CopilotPkgCommand auth login --provider copilot }
1202	        }
1203	        'reinstall' {
1204	            # Force a clean re-install of the pinned spec (normally only needed if the
1205	            # prefix got corrupted — a version bump re-installs on its own via the stamp).
1206	            Write-Host "copilot-proxy: removing $(Get-CopilotPkgPrefix) ..."
1207	            Remove-Item -Recurse -Force (Get-CopilotPkgPrefix) -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
1208	            if (-not (Install-CopilotPkg)) { return }
1209	            $installed = Get-CopilotPkgMetadata
1210	            Write-Host "copilot-proxy: installed $($installed.Name)@$($installed.Version) (requested $(Get-CopilotPkg)) -> $(Get-CopilotPkgPrefix)"
1211	        }
1212	        { $_ -in 'whoami', 'usage' } {
1213	            if (-not (Test-Path (Get-CopilotToken))) { Write-Error "copilot-proxy: not authenticated — run 'copilot-proxy auth'."; return }
1214	            if ((Get-CopilotPkgFlavor) -eq 'original') {
1215	                Invoke-CopilotPkgCommand check-usage
1216	            }
1217	            elseif (Test-CopilotAlive) {
1218	                try {
1219	                    $u = Invoke-RestMethod -Uri "$(Get-CopilotBase)/usage" -TimeoutSec 5 -ErrorAction Stop
1220	                    [pscustomobject]@{
1221	                        plan        = if ($u.copilot_plan) { $u.copilot_plan } elseif ($u.access_type_sku) { $u.access_type_sku } else { 'unknown' }
1222	                        quota_reset = $u.quota_reset_date
1223	                        quotas      = $u.quota_snapshots
1224	                    } | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 6
1225	                } catch { Write-Error "copilot-proxy: /usage query failed: $_" }
1226	            } else {
1227	                Write-Host "copilot-proxy: not running — showing auth/debug info instead of quota."
1228	                Invoke-CopilotPkgCommand debug
1229	            }
1230	        }
1231	        'shim' {
1232	            $sf = Get-CopilotShimState
1233	            $sub = if ($Argv.Count -ge 2) { $Argv[1] } else { 'status' }
1234	            switch ($sub) {
1235	                'on' {
1236	                    New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path (Split-Path $sf) | Out-Null
1237	                    'on' | Set-Content $sf
1238	                    if (Test-CopilotAlive) { if (Start-CopilotShim) { Write-Host "copilot-proxy: shim ON -> $(Get-CopilotShimBase) (-> $(Get-CopilotBase))" } }
1239	                    else { Write-Host "copilot-proxy: shim enabled; will start with the proxy." }

1	#!/usr/bin/env bun
2	// copilot-throttle-shim.js — a tiny streaming reverse proxy that sits IN FRONT
3	// of the local copilot-api fork (default :4141). It provides the request
4	// compatibility fixes shared by Codex/Claude Code and stops GitHub's enterprise
5	// Copilot backend from 403-ing ("Forbidden") on bursts of premium requests,
6	// WITHOUT adding latency to normal single-agent flow.
7	//
8	//   agent client ─▶ shim (:4142) ─▶ copilot-api fork (:4141) ─▶ Copilot backend
9	//                    │
10	//                    ├─ semaphore: at most MAX concurrent in-flight upstream
11	//                    │   POSTs; a burst queues instead of hitting the backend
12	//                    │   all at once (that simultaneity is what trips abuse
13	//                    │   detection). Under the cap there is ZERO added latency.
14	//                    │
15	//                    └─ transparent retry on 403/429/502/503/504 + network
16	//                        errors, jittered backoff, BEFORE any response body is
17	//                        streamed — so the agent never sees the transient 403
18	//                        ("Please run /login"). GET/HEAD (health, /v1/models)
19	//                        bypass both, so liveness checks stay instant.
20	//
21	// Managed by copilot-proxy (see 43_copilot_proxy.sh: `copilot-proxy shim on`).
22	// Config via env (all optional):
23	//   COPILOT_SHIM_PORT       listen port                    (default 4142)
24	//   COPILOT_SHIM_UPSTREAM   upstream base URL              (default http://localhost:4141)
25	//   COPILOT_SHIM_MAX        max concurrent in-flight POSTs (default 4)
26	//   COPILOT_SHIM_RETRIES    retry attempts on transient    (default 3)
27	//   COPILOT_SHIM_BACKOFF_MS base backoff ms, doubles/try   (default 500)
28	
29	const PORT = Number(process.env.COPILOT_SHIM_PORT ?? 4142);
30	const UPSTREAM = (process.env.COPILOT_SHIM_UPSTREAM ?? "http://localhost:4141").replace(/\/+$/, "");
31	const MAX = Math.max(1, Number(process.env.COPILOT_SHIM_MAX ?? 4));
32	const RETRIES = Math.max(0, Number(process.env.COPILOT_SHIM_RETRIES ?? 3));
33	const BACKOFF_MS = Math.max(0, Number(process.env.COPILOT_SHIM_BACKOFF_MS ?? 500));
34	const RETRY_STATUS = new Set([403, 429, 502, 503, 504]);
35	
36	const log = (...a) => console.log(new Date().toISOString(), "[shim]", ...a);
37	const sleep = (ms) => new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, ms));
38	
39	// ---- semaphore (at most MAX permits; hands a permit straight to a waiter) ----
40	let active = 0;
41	const waiters = [];
42	function acquire() {
43	  if (active < MAX) { active++; return Promise.resolve(); }
44	  return new Promise((res) => waiters.push(res));
45	}
46	function release() {
47	  active--;
48	  const next = waiters.shift();
49	  if (next) { active++; next(); }
50	}
51	
52	function backoffMs(attempt, retryAfter) {
53	  const ra = Number(retryAfter);
54	  if (Number.isFinite(ra) && ra > 0) return Math.min(ra * 1000, 30000);
55	  return BACKOFF_MS * 2 ** attempt + Math.floor(Math.random() * BACKOFF_MS); // + jitter
56	}

58	function buildUpstream(req, bodyBuf, bodyWasDecoded = false) {
59	  const url = new URL(req.url);
60	  const target = UPSTREAM + url.pathname + url.search;
61	  const headers = new Headers(req.headers);
62	  headers.delete("host");
63	  headers.delete("content-length"); // fetch recomputes from body
64	  if (bodyWasDecoded) headers.delete("content-encoding");
65	  const init = { method: req.method, headers, signal: req.signal };
66	  if (bodyBuf !== undefined) init.body = bodyBuf;
67	  return { target, init };
68	}

70	function blankDescription(value) {
71	  return typeof value !== "string" || value.trim().length === 0;
72	}

74	function toolLabel(tool) {
75	  const name = tool?.name ?? tool?.tool_name ?? tool?.title;
76	  return typeof name === "string" && name.trim() ? name.trim() : "unnamed tool";

79	// Codex records MCP discovery in Responses input items. Some MCP/plugin
80	// servers legally omit a tool description, which Codex serializes as "". The
81	// GitHub Copilot Responses endpoint is stricter than OpenAI's endpoint and
82	// rejects that request before inference:
83	//
84	//   Invalid 'input[0].tools[0].description': empty string.
85	//
86	// Only touch tool-definition arrays in the two Responses locations Codex uses;
87	// do not recursively rewrite user input, JSON Schema descriptions, or outputs.
88	export function normalizeResponsesToolDescriptions(payload) {
89	  let changed = 0;
90	  const patched = [];
91	
92	  const normalizeTools = (tools, prefix, requireDescriptionField = false) => {
93	    if (!Array.isArray(tools)) return;
94	    tools.forEach((tool, index) => {
95	      if (!tool || typeof tool !== "object") return;
96	      if (requireDescriptionField && !("description" in tool)) return;
97	      if (!blankDescription(tool.description)) return;
98	      const label = toolLabel(tool);
99	      tool.description = `Tool ${label}.`;
100	      changed++;
101	      patched.push(`${prefix}[${index}].description`);
102	    });
103	  };
104	
105	  if (!payload || typeof payload !== "object") return { changed, patched };
106	  // Built-in top-level tools such as web_search do not have a description by
107	  // design, so only repair an explicitly present-but-blank field there.
108	  normalizeTools(payload.tools, "tools", true);
109	  if (Array.isArray(payload.input)) {
110	    payload.input.forEach((item, index) => {
111	      // Codex versions have used more than one discriminator for persisted MCP
112	      // discovery. The stable shape is the nested tool-definition array itself.
113	      if (!item || typeof item !== "object") return;
114	      normalizeTools(item.tools, `input[${index}].tools`);
115	    });
116	  }
117	  return { changed, patched };
118	}

120	export function normalizeRequestBody(pathname, bodyBuf, contentEncoding = "") {
121	  if (pathname !== "/responses" && pathname !== "/v1/responses") {
122	    return { body: bodyBuf, changed: 0, patched: [], parseError: null, decoded: false };
123	  }
124	  try {
125	    const encoding = contentEncoding.trim().toLowerCase();
126	    const decodedBody = encoding === "zstd" ? Bun.zstdDecompressSync(new Uint8Array(bodyBuf)) : bodyBuf;
127	    const payload = JSON.parse(new TextDecoder().decode(decodedBody));
128	    const result = normalizeResponsesToolDescriptions(payload);
129	    if (result.changed === 0) return { body: bodyBuf, ...result, parseError: null, decoded: false };
130	    return { body: JSON.stringify(payload), ...result, parseError: null, decoded: encoding === "zstd" };
131	  } catch (error) {
132	    // Preserve malformed/non-JSON requests verbatim; the upstream remains the
133	    // authority for their validation and error response.
134	    return { body: bodyBuf, changed: 0, patched: [], parseError: String(error), decoded: false };
135	  }

139	// the stream ends / errors / is cancelled (true in-flight accounting).
140	function streamThrough(resp, releaseOnce) {
141	  const headers = new Headers(resp.headers);
142	  headers.delete("content-encoding");  // Bun already decoded the upstream body
143	  headers.delete("content-length");
144	  headers.delete("transfer-encoding");
145	  if (!resp.body) { releaseOnce(); return new Response(null, { status: resp.status, headers }); }
146	
147	  const reader = resp.body.getReader();
148	  const stream = new ReadableStream({
149	    async pull(controller) {
150	      try {
151	        const { done, value } = await reader.read();
152	        if (done) { controller.close(); releaseOnce(); return; }
153	        controller.enqueue(value);
154	      } catch (err) { releaseOnce(); controller.error(err); }
155	    },
156	    cancel(reason) { releaseOnce(); try { reader.cancel(reason); } catch {} },
157	  });
158	  return new Response(stream, { status: resp.status, headers });
159	}
160	
161	export function startServer() {
162	  const server = Bun.serve({
163	    port: PORT,
164	    idleTimeout: 255, // seconds — long opus streams (saw up to ~77s)
165	    async fetch(req) {
166	    const url = new URL(req.url);
167	    const method = req.method;
168	
169	    // Health / metadata reads: straight passthrough, no permit, no retry.
170	    if (method === "GET" || method === "HEAD") {
171	      try {
172	        const { target, init } = buildUpstream(req, undefined);
173	        return streamThrough(await fetch(target, init), () => {});
174	      } catch (err) {
175	        return new Response(`shim: upstream unreachable: ${err}`, { status: 502 });
176	      }
177	    }
178	
179	    // Mutating requests (POST /v1/messages …): buffer body so we can resend on
180	    // retry, then throttle + retry.
181	    const bodyBuf = await req.arrayBuffer();
182	    const normalized = normalizeRequestBody(url.pathname, bodyBuf, req.headers.get("content-encoding") ?? "");
183	    if (normalized.parseError) {
184	      log(`${method} ${url.pathname} could not inspect JSON (${bodyBuf.byteLength} bytes, content-type=${req.headers.get("content-type") ?? "unset"}, content-encoding=${req.headers.get("content-encoding") ?? "unset"}): ${normalized.parseError}`);
185	    }
186	    if (normalized.changed > 0) {
187	      log(`${method} ${url.pathname} filled ${normalized.changed} empty tool description(s): ${normalized.patched.join(", ")}`);
188	    }
189	    const { target, init } = buildUpstream(req, normalized.body, normalized.decoded);
190	
191	    const willQueue = active >= MAX;
192	    await acquire();
193	    if (willQueue) log(`queued ${method} ${url.pathname} (${active} in-flight, ${waiters.length} waiting)`);
194	    let released = false;
195	    const releaseOnce = () => { if (!released) { released = true; release(); } };
196	
197	    try {
198	      for (let attempt = 0; attempt <= RETRIES; attempt++) {
199	        let resp;
200	        try {
201	          resp = await fetch(target, init);
202	        } catch (err) {
203	          if (req.signal?.aborted) { releaseOnce(); return new Response("client aborted", { status: 499 }); }
204	          if (attempt < RETRIES) {
205	            const d = backoffMs(attempt);
206	            log(`${method} ${url.pathname} network error (${err}); retry ${attempt + 1}/${RETRIES} in ${d}ms`);
207	            await sleep(d);
208	            continue;
209	          }
210	          releaseOnce();
211	          return new Response(`shim: upstream unreachable: ${err}`, { status: 502 });
212	        }
213	
214	        // Retryable status and attempts left → back off and try again. The 403
215	        // arrives fast (<2s, before any body), so retrying here is safe.
216	        if (RETRY_STATUS.has(resp.status) && attempt < RETRIES) {
217	          const d = backoffMs(attempt, resp.headers.get("retry-after"));
218	          log(`${method} ${url.pathname} -> ${resp.status}; retry ${attempt + 1}/${RETRIES} in ${d}ms`);
219	          try { await resp.body?.cancel(); } catch {}
220	          await sleep(d);
221	          continue;
222	        }
223	
224	        // Commit: stream this response (2xx, or the real error after retries).
225	        if (attempt > 0) log(`${method} ${url.pathname} -> ${resp.status} after ${attempt} retr${attempt === 1 ? "y" : "ies"}`);
226	        return streamThrough(resp, releaseOnce);
227	      }
228	      releaseOnce(); // unreachable (last attempt always commits) — safety net
229	      return new Response("shim: retries exhausted", { status: 502 });
230	    } catch (err) {
231	      releaseOnce();
232	      return new Response(`shim: ${err}`, { status: 500 });
233	    }
234	    },
235	  });
236	
237	  log(`listening on :${server.port} -> ${UPSTREAM} (max=${MAX}, retries=${RETRIES}, backoff=${BACKOFF_MS}ms)`);
238	  return server;
239	}
240	
241	if (import.meta.main) startServer();
242

2. Require the saved GitHub token:
   - lines 617–621
3. Rotate three generations of logs:
   - lines 622–630
4. Install the pinned package once if necessary:
   - lines 631–634
   - package prefix/stamp logic is at lines 126–245
5. Resolve direct versus local HTTP proxy egress:
   - lines 635–648

   - original package with `--rate-limit --wait`, lines 650–670
   - maintained fork with optional `--proxy-env`, lines 671–686
7. Poll `/v1/models` for up to `COPILOT_PROXY_START_TIMEOUT`, default 45 seconds:

`claude-copilot` delegates to `copilot-run`:

   - lines 1262–1272.

An active project `settings.local.json` pin can still outrank this inherited environment, as documented at lines 37–47 and 1220–1224.

`codex-copilot`:

# 3. Exact candidate ordering

## Claude Code `copilot-model --auto`

Implemented at `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/shell/43_copilot_proxy.sh:1932-1976`.

All candidates first have a trailing `[1m]` stripped.

### Fixed Claude order

1. `claude-fable-5`
2. `claude-opus-5`
3. `claude-opus-4-8`
4. `claude-opus-4-7`
5. `claude-opus-4-6`
6. `claude-sonnet-5`
7. `claude-sonnet-4-6`
8. `claude-sonnet-4-5`
9. `claude-opus-4-5`
10. `claude-haiku-4-5`

Then the lexicographically greatest remaining `claude-*` ID.

The documentation’s shorthand “Fable > Opus > Sonnet > Haiku” is not exact: `claude-opus-4-5` intentionally follows the named Sonnet models.

### Fixed OpenAI order

1. `gpt-5.6-sol`
2. `gpt-5.6-terra`
3. `gpt-5.5`
4. `gpt-5.4`
5. `gpt-5.3-codex`
6. `gpt-5.6-luna`
7. `gpt-5.4-mini`
8. `gpt-5-mini`

Then:

1. lexicographically greatest `gpt-*` excluding `mini|nano|luna`
2. lexicographically greatest ID containing `codex`
3. lexicographically greatest remaining `gpt-*`

### Gemini and final fallback

1. Lexicographically greatest non-Flash `gemini-*`
2. Lexicographically greatest `gemini-*`
3. Lexicographically greatest model of any kind

This is ID/name ranking, not capability-field scoring.

## Codex auto ordering

Implemented at lines 1280–1323.

Codex uses the same fixed OpenAI list first, then generic GPT/Codex fallbacks, then the same fixed Claude list, then Gemini, then arbitrary fallback.

The key difference is therefore:

- Claude Code: Claude → OpenAI → Gemini → other
- Codex: OpenAI → Claude → Gemini → other

Codex’s catalog input is filtered at lines 1413–1418 for:

- `policy.state != disabled`
- `model_picker_enabled != false`
- non-embedding capability type

The Claude picker does not apply these filters.

## Role-profile ordering

Implemented at lines 1982–2032.

### Native Claude main

For each role:

- Fable: `claude-fable-5`, then greatest `claude-fable-*`, then main
- Opus: Opus 5 → 4.8 → 4.7 → 4.6 → 4.5, then greatest Opus, then main
- Sonnet: Sonnet 5 → 4.6 → 4.5, then greatest Sonnet, then main
- Haiku: Haiku 4.5, then greatest Haiku, then main

### GPT/Codex main

- Main: selected model
- Fable: selected model
- Opus: selected model
- Sonnet: `gpt-5.6-terra`, otherwise selected model
- Haiku/background:
  1. `gpt-5.6-luna`
  2. `gpt-5.4-mini`
  3. `gpt-5-mini`
  4. selected model

### Other provider

All roles use the selected main.

# 4. Model ID and `[1m]` handling

## Three model-ID views

The implementation correctly distinguishes:

1. **Raw gateway ID**  
   Example: `gpt-5.6-sol` or `claude-opus-4-8`.

2. **Claude-facing ID**  
   Example: `gpt-5.6-sol[1m]`.

3. **Cross-source comparison key**  
   Lowercase, dots changed to dashes, `[1m]` stripped.

## Cross-source normalization

`_copilot_norm_models` at lines 558–563 performs:

```text
uppercase → lowercase
"." → "-"
trailing "[1m]" → removed
sort -u
```

It is designed to fold:

- upstream `claude-opus-4.8`
- proxy raw `claude-opus-4-8`
- proxy alias `claude-opus-4-8[1m]`

into one key.

However, it is currently dead production code; see finding 1 below.

## Manual fuzzy normalization

`copilot-model` uses a different, much narrower normalization at lines 2180–2207:

- strips explicit `[1m]`
- changes dots to dashes
- tries exact input
- tries `claude-` prefix
- tries normalized input
- tries normalized `claude-` prefix
- finally requires a unique substring match

It does not lowercase input. `_copilot_norm_models`’ lowercasing therefore does not make manual `copilot-model` matching case-insensitive.

## Context hint generation

`_copilot_model_for_claude`, lines 1892–1914:

- strips existing `[1m]`
- finds the raw ID in `.data[].id`
- reads `.capabilities.limits.max_context_window_tokens`
- appends `[1m]` when the value is numeric and `>= 1000000`
- removes the hint when live metadata says less than 1M
- preserves an explicit stored hint only when there is no live catalog

Every role is passed through this function at lines 2025–2031.

## Display handling

The proxy script itself does not produce friendly Claude HUD names. The display chain is documented at:

- `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/pitfalls/claude-hud-shows-raw-model-id.md:31-53`
- `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/docs/tools/claude-hud.md:208-209`
- `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/docs/tools/claude-hud.md:233-235`

Claude Code supplies `model.display_name`; claude-hud uses it when present and otherwise falls back to raw `model.id`. An old Claude Code binary that does not recognize an ID can therefore show literal `claude-opus-5[1m]` and use the wrong context size.

Raycast has separate display logic:

- `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/shell/45_copilot_raycast.sh:186-208` chooses `.name`, then `.display_name`, then `.id`.
- Lines 382–398 append `" (Copilot)"` and emit integer context.

Codex display/metadata is preserved with the bundled catalog override rather than by changing the model string.

# 6. Likely bugs and gaps

## High confidence

### 1. Exact stale-cache detection was accidentally disconnected

Current state:

- `_copilot_norm_models` exists at  
  `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/shell/43_copilot_proxy.sh:558-563`.
- It is called only by  
  `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/tests/unit/copilot_proxy.bats:84-125`.
- Production doctor only compares counts/presence at  
  `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/shell/43_copilot_proxy.sh:860-907`.

Consequences:

- If upstream has eight Claude models and the process has one stale Claude model, doctor reports:
  - `"served Claude list looks healthy"`
- If no local HTTP proxy is configured, direct upstream has Claude, but the running cache has none, none of the current cache-verdict branches necessarily fires.
- A newly added upstream model missing from the process cache is invisible as long as some Claude ID remains.

History confirms this is a regression:

- Commit `bf6cc2f` originally used `_copilot_norm_models` to compute exact upstream-minus-served IDs.
- Commit `1a2be50` replaced that block with direct-vs-proxy Claude counts but left the helper and tests behind.

Documentation is now overstated:

- `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/docs/tools/copilot-claude-proxy.md:169-181`
- `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/pitfalls/README.md:138`

The latter explicitly says doctor “diffs cached vs live upstream list,” which current code does not do.

### 2. Claude auto-selection accepts ineligible and embedding IDs

`_copilot_catalog_ids` emits every raw `.data[].id`:

- `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/shell/43_copilot_proxy.sh:1880-1885`

`copilot-model --auto` feeds that unfiltered set into the picker:

- lines 2143–2160

The final picker fallback returns the lexicographically greatest arbitrary ID:

- line 1975

A pure invocation with only `text-embedding-3-small` selected that embedding model.

Codex applies eligibility filters at lines 1413–1418; Claude does not.

The adjacent Raycast implementation makes the larger issue explicit:

- `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/shell/45_copilot_raycast.sh:25-37`
- `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/docs/tools/raycast-ai-byok.md:185-208`

That documentation records models advertised with `model_picker_enabled: true` and `policy.state: enabled` that still return `model_not_supported`. Thus even copying Codex’s filters would not fully establish usability; a Messages-compatible entitlement probe or safer eligibility contract would be needed.

### 3. Explicit Codex models miss live context and compaction limits

At:

- `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/shell/43_copilot_proxy.sh:1383`
- lines 1409–1429

an explicit `-m` or `--model` sets `explicit_model=1`, but the internal `model` variable remains empty.

Limit extraction is guarded by:

- lines 1437–1442: `if [ -n "$model" ]`

Therefore explicit models do not receive:

- `model_context_window`
- `model_auto_compact_token_limit`

Only auto-selected models do.

This contradicts the broad documentation claim at:

- `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/docs/tools/copilot-claude-proxy.md:282-294`
- `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/pitfalls/codex-model-metadata-not-found-after-copilot-refresh.md:63-66`

The explicit-model test at lines 351–369 checks model preservation and catalog pinning but does not assert live limits.

### 4. Project-pin ownership is inferred from any base URL

The following all treat any nonempty `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` as a Copilot-owned pin:

- effective model: `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/shell/43_copilot_proxy.sh:383-388`
- doctor role profile: lines 923–935
- `copilot-here status`: lines 1712–1720
- one-shot prior-pin detection: lines 1766–1771

A project configured for another Anthropic-compatible gateway can therefore be:

The test named “WITHOUT our base_url is not a pin” at lines 246–256 only tests an entirely absent base URL, not a foreign URL. There is no ownership marker or recognized-base comparison.

The tests define:

and expect Luna without `[1m]`:

## Medium confidence or design gaps

### 6. Manual `[1m]` can override contradictory live metadata

The helper itself correctly removes `[1m]` when live context is below 1M:

- `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/shell/43_copilot_proxy.sh:1895-1913`

But manual `copilot-model 'id[1m]'` bypasses the helper after validation and unconditionally re-appends the suffix:

- lines 2180–2212

Thus `copilot-model 'gpt-5.6-luna[1m]'` can persist a false 1M hint even if live metadata says 400k. This may be intended as an expert override, but it conflicts with the stated metadata-derived safety model and is untested.

### 7. `[1m]` transport semantics are contradictory

The code says the gateway accepts both raw `.id` and `.claude_model_id`, with the latter carrying the suffix Claude Code sends:

- `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/shell/43_copilot_proxy.sh:363-370`

Elsewhere it says a raw API client must avoid `[1m]` because the proxy rejects it:

- lines 1076–1082
- `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/docs/tools/copilot-claude-proxy.md:627-629`
- `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/docs/tools/raycast-ai-byok.md:206-208`

The main documentation also says Claude Code strips the suffix before sending, whereas the implementation comment says it sends the alias. This might be endpoint-specific behavior, but that distinction is not documented or tested.

### 8. Doctor’s live probe does not probe the effective pinned model

At:

- `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/shell/43_copilot_proxy.sh:1076-1095`

doctor selects the first sorted non-embedding, non-`[1m]` ID. It does not use `_copilot_effective_model`.

Consequences:

- a valid pinned Sol model can be blamed because some unrelated first Claude ID is unusable
- a bad pinned model may be missed if a different first model succeeds
- it does not prove the role aliases work

The default doctor does list validation only; `--live` still does not close that gap.

### 9. Claude “auto” is a one-time selector, not an ongoing mode

`copilot-model --auto` resolves one model and writes its ID. It does not store an auto-policy marker.

After catalog/entitlement changes:

- wrappers keep using the saved model
- role tiers may be recomputed, but the main is not reselected
- doctor advises rerunning `copilot-model --auto`

Codex, by contrast, performs live auto-selection on every `codex-copilot` invocation.

There is also no request-time provider/model retry. “Fallback” currently means:

- picker candidate fallback
- missing role tier → selected main
- static offline list for manual discovery
- shim-down → direct proxy base URL

It does not mean automatic inference failover after `model_not_supported`, 401, or a transport failure.

### 10. `COPILOT_CLAUDE_MODEL` can make `copilot-model` writes ineffective

`COPILOT_CLAUDE_MODEL` outranks the state file at lines 346–354.

However, global `copilot-model` still writes the state file at lines 2252–2257 and prints an apparent transition. With the environment variable still set, the next wrapper continues using the environment value, not the newly written state.

Related display issue:

- `copilot-model -c` prints `global main: <state-file-path>` at lines 2125–2128 even when the actual source is the environment or built-in default.
- The main documentation claims `-c` shows the source layer at `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/docs/tools/copilot-claude-proxy.md:386-387`.

`_copilot_effective_model` already computes accurate source labels, but `copilot-model -c` does not use it.

### 11. Generic fallback ordering is lexical and misses OpenAI `o*` families

Both pickers use plain lexical `sort | tail -1` for generic IDs.

That means:

- future `4-10` versus `4-9` IDs may order incorrectly
- unknown product tiers are not compared by capabilities
- `o1`, `o3`, and `o4` are not classified as OpenAI by either picker

A pure call with `o3` and `gemini-3.1-pro-preview` selected Gemini in both selectors, despite documentation saying OpenAI precedes Gemini. Raycast’s temperature logic does explicitly recognize `o1/o3/o4` at:

- `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/shell/45_copilot_raycast.sh:162-171`

### 12. “Capability-ranked” is overstated

The selectors do not score:

- context
- prompt limit
- vision
- tools
- reasoning effort
- endpoint support

They rank hard-coded product names and then apply lexical fallback. Capability metadata is used after selection for:

- Claude `[1m]`
- Codex context/compaction limits
- Raycast display abilities

Calling the main selection “capability-ranked” is therefore product-tier shorthand, not dynamic capability ranking.

### 13. Raycast ranks Fable below Haiku

At:

- `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/shell/45_copilot_raycast.sh:144-159`

the ranks are:

- Opus: 59
- Sonnet: 58
- Haiku: 57
- any other Claude, including Fable: 56

Thus `claude-fable-5` displays below Haiku even though the main selector explicitly ranks Fable first. There is no Raycast test coverage.

Raycast also silently substitutes `128000` when context is absent, invalid, or zero:

- lines 383–398

That keeps the YAML loadable but may misrepresent the actual model context without warning.

### 14. Doctor does not validate the legacy small-fast alias

The generated environment sets `ANTHROPIC_SMALL_FAST_MODEL` equal to Haiku:

- `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/shell/43_copilot_proxy.sh:1608-1621`
- lines 1262–1271

Doctor extracts and validates Fable, Opus, Sonnet, and Haiku only:

- lines 923–957

A stale `ANTHROPIC_SMALL_FAST_MODEL` in an older or hand-edited project pin is not checked.
